issues.body:
TX-SCOPE-001 (line 258-259) reads: "A certification MUST identify its issuer, framework, scope, validity interval, certifying authority, and verifiable attestation binding."

Section 6 is titled "Normative Trust Expression vocabulary" and presents its table as the enumeration of normative terms. That table supplies a term for four of the six elements — issuer (trustx:certifies), framework (trustx:underFramework), scope (trustx:scope), validity interval (trustx:validFrom/validUntil) — but there is NO term for "certifying authority" and none for "verifiable attestation binding". Neither appears anywhere else in the document: the only prov: predicate used is prov:wasAttributedTo, and it is introduced only for status attestations (line 199) and for the response reifier (line 281/293), never for a trustx:Certification. The section 7.1 certification example likewise carries only `a trustx:Certification ; trustx:certifies ...`.

Consequence: two of the six sub-clauses of a normative MUST are not expressible in the vocabulary the document defines, so they are untestable and two conforming implementations can carry them in incompatible ways. This also weakens TX-EVAL-002's MUST to "independently check ... signatures", since the response has no defined place to put the binding being checked, and section 10's conformance list has no signature/authority case.

Rated minor rather than major: the draft is explicit that "Issuer-to-key binding is an external trust anchor" (line ~151) and that it "defines data shapes and fail-closed verification obligations, not a cryptographic guarantee", so the omission is adjacent to a disclosed scope boundary rather than a soundness hole in shipped code.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) add the two missing terms to the section-6 table — e.g. a trustx:certifiedBy (or a normative reuse of prov:wasAttributedTo on the certification) for the certifying authority, and a trustx:attestation / proof predicate for the verifiable binding — and show them in the section-7.1 certification example, disclosing under the table whether either has a framework_vocab constant yet; or (b) reword TX-SCOPE-001 to say the certifying authority is identified by prov:wasAttributedTo and that the attestation binding is carried out of band by the external trust anchor of section 4.3, explicitly out of scope for this vocabulary. Option (b) is the smaller change and matches the draft's stated scope.
issues.title: TX-SCOPE-001 MUSTs two certification elements the normative vocabulary defines no term for

issues.body:
Section 4.1 defines the disjunction per statement: "a contributing statement is admissible when it satisfies every condition of at least one resource. Conditions within one resource are AND-combined."

TX-EVAL-001 (line ~330) instead reads: "A holder MUST evaluate Q only over statements satisfying one complete requirements resource." The natural reading of "one complete requirements resource" is a single shared resource that all contributing statements satisfy, which is strictly narrower than 4.1: given statement A satisfying only R1 and statement B satisfying only R2, 4.1 admits both while the narrow reading of TX-EVAL-001 admits neither combination.

Section 4.5's "A holder MUST NOT combine a partially satisfied direct requirement with a partially satisfied framework requirement" is about partial satisfaction and does not settle which reading is intended — if anything it leans toward the narrow one. Since TX-EVAL-001 is the normative evaluation rule, the ambiguity is worth closing.
issues.fix_hint: Reword TX-EVAL-001 to match whichever is intended, e.g. per-statement: "MUST evaluate Q only over statements that each satisfy every condition of at least one requirements resource (section 4.1)"; or per-answer: "MUST evaluate Q only over statements that all satisfy every condition of the same single requirements resource". Add the corresponding conformance case to section 10 (two resources, each satisfied by a different contributing statement).
issues.title: TX-EVAL-001 restates the multi-resource disjunction more narrowly than section 4.1 defines it

verdict.summary:
Round-3 review of PR #4199 (new Unofficial Proposal Draft site/specs/trust-expression.typ + its specs.ts registry entry), verified against the checkout at head e957b20f.

NOTE ON PROGRESS: no commit has landed since round 2 reviewed this head, so nothing in the PR got worse. I mark "regressing" only because the literal scale counts NEW findings, and my pass surfaced one minor and one nit that round 2 did not record, while round 2's single nit remains unaddressed. This is added reviewer coverage, not code regression.

RE-VERIFIED round-1/round-2 fixes, all still good: trustx: binds to https://sparq.dev/ns/trust#, matching framework_vocab.rs:61 TRUSTX_NS. Inclusive-endpoint wording matches graph.rs:342-350 GATE 4 (rejects only now < valid_from || now > valid_until) and the "(inclusive)" doc comments at graph.rs:174/176. Every cited symbol exists and has the stated visibility: verify_manifest (verifier.rs:5623, pub), ProofManifest (manifest.rs:1655), sparq_zk_compose::revocation (lib.rs:42), SignedStatusList (394), VerifyingLiveStatusCheck (460), justify_status_decision (629), desugar_for_predicate (vocab.rs:138), admissible (admissibility.rs:210), secprop (lib.rs:149), SEC_REQ_EIDAS20/SEC_REQ_UK_DVS. sparq_core::nt is `mod nt;` (private) and is honestly described as internal. The disclosure that exactly trustx:credential/status/valid lack constants is accurate — I diffed the table against framework_vocab.rs and the rest all ship.

MECHANICS: both build-boundary honesty gates pass on this source (check-no-perf-numbers 0 findings; check-privacy-claims OK over 742 files). The specs.ts registry parses cleanly under build-specs.mjs readRegistry — all seven parallel-array fields return 7 entries, aligned. Routes/e2e are data-driven off SPECS, so the new slug is auto-covered. Preamble and #table/table.header usage match the house pattern in the six sibling specs.

No blocker or major issue; ZK/MPC standing is caveated throughout (sq-qhy4 named, MPC semi-honest-only).
